bull.b: Natera has moved to materially positive cash generation, with TTM operating cash flow ~ $211M and FCF ~ $92M. Durable positive cash flow improves runway for R&D and commercial expansion, reduces refinancing risk, and supports reinvestment without relying solely on equity raises.

Broad-based volume and revenue acceleration — including record quarterly revenue and a >1M annualized MRD run rate — indicate scalable demand for Signatera and women's health products, strengthening durable revenue growth as adoption and clinician reliance expand.

bull.t: High gross margins and raised guidance
bull.b: Sustained gross margins near 65% reflect favorable unit economics for molecular assays and operating leverage as volumes scale. Management's upward margin and revenue guidance signals structural improvement in profitability potential beyond transient quarter timing effects.

bear.b: Despite revenue scale and margins, the company remains unprofitable with negative EBIT and ROE, meaning it still must convert margin strength into sustained operating profits. Persistent losses can constrain long-term returns and limit capital allocation flexibility if not corrected.

Incomplete Medicare/commercial coverage and prior-authorization hurdles can structurally slow adoption and cash realization for diagnostic tests. Ongoing payer work increases revenue uncertainty and can cap addressable volume growth until reimbursement expands.

bear.t: Equity plan increase may dilute shareholders
bear.b: Approval to expand the equity award pool supports retention but introduces dilution risk to existing holders. Over multiple grant cycles, expanded share issuance can offset EPS gains from revenue growth and complicate long-term per-share value accretion.
